content:
maya: FYI seeing a sharp CPU + p99 tail on host-proxy after the proxy change this morning. Looks correlated with a spike in very small streaming requests (50-300B payloads).
liam: timeline? which deploy/tag?
deploy-bot: Deployed proxy-v3.8.1 at 2026-03-18T09:12:03Z by ci/canary
maya: proxy-v3.8.1 yes. roll-forward from v3.8.0. believed safe, but perf dashboards show write syscalls skyrocketing.
arjun: any flamegraphs / pprof? quick suspicion: header handling or http2 framing because the model-side payloads are tiny but many.
maya: attaching quick pprof snapshot (verbatim lines):

--- begin pprof ---
1000ms total
  42%  host_proxy  writev
  18%  host_proxy  http2: writeFrame
  12%  host_proxy  headerEncode
  10%  host_proxy  serializeHeaders
   8%  runtime     netpoll
--- end pprof ---

nora: writev/frames dominate — that's consistent with many small frames. Did we change header processing/hpack code in v3.8.1? liam?
liam: v3.8.1 introduced a change to aggressively split header blocks to avoid large header compression churn across multiplexed streams. But it shouldn't increase syscall count like this.
arjun: could be a bug where we end up emitting headers per chunk rather than coalescing into one header frame per request. If streaming chunks trigger header re-emit prelude then we get N small writes.
maya: repro script: send 2000 concurrent tiny streaming requests (5k qps) with single-stream chunked responses. Observed avg write calls/request increased from ~3 to ~18.
liam: can you paste a minimal curl/golang repro?
maya: here's a simplified client: ```go
// sends Metadata then small json body, then half-close
conn := http2.ClientConn(...)
for i := 0; i < N; i++ {
  req := &http.Request{Method: "POST", URL: url, Body: bytes.NewReader([]byte("{}"))}
  resp, _ := client.Do(req)
  // read streaming chunks
}
```

nora: on the host side, headers and chunk preface look like:
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.test
content-type: application/json
x-client-id: c-123
```
But in the trace we see the proxy emitting this header block multiple times mid-stream with each mini-chunk.
liam: hmm. that matches the change — we attempted to emit a CONTINUATION only when the header block exceeded X bytes. But a race with chunking caused us to re-encode headers for each chunk.
arjun: quick mitigation: make header encode be idempotent and cached per-stream until stream close. Or simply force coalescing: buffer header block until first body write flush.
maya: measured impact of simple mitigation (cache header block): write syscalls dropped 4.5x, CPU p99 returned to baseline in our canary.
liam: nice. any downstream impact? HPACK table memory growth? arjun?
arjun: caching header block per stream is cheap (a few hundred bytes). HPACK dynamic table is separate; our change doesn't alter dynamic table updates. But we must avoid unbounded cache growth — free on stream close.
nora: we should also add a unit test exercising interleaved header/body writes to prevent regressions.
liam: agree. action items:
- revert risky header-splitting change in v3.8.1 (short-term rollback) (owner: liam)
- implement header-block caching per-stream + test (owner: arjun)
- add e2e perf check: synthetic 5k qps tiny streaming workload to CI perf (owner: maya)
- add tracing tag/metric for per-request header encode count (owner: nora)

maya: I filed a short incident ticket: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0318
liam: I'll open the PR to revert with patch and include the pprof snippet + microbench.
arjun: also let's add a small change to grpc/http2 outbound path: accumulate header frames into a single buffer before calling writev. That prevents small-syscall storms when multiple goroutines race to write.
maya: non-blocking question: could KV cache behavior be compounding this? e.g., extra header re-emits causing KVCACHE misses because request ids moved? anyone saw kv spikes?
nora: KVCACHE metrics show a small uptick in invalidations around the same window but not huge. Most of the cost is in host CPU syscalls. KV thrash is secondary.
liam: good. plan: revert ASAP, then land caching+coalesce in follow-up. Roll for canaries first.

deploy-bot: Started rollback of proxy-v3.8.0 at 2026-03-18T09:28:12Z
maya: monitoring canary now, thank you. will post perf delta in ~10m.
liam: once stable, let's add a small benchmark to eng-runtime perf-suite that specifically sends many tiny streaming payloads and asserts writev count < threshold.
maya: noted — I'll add it.
nora: PR checklist: unit tests, e2e perf, trace metric, changelog entry explaining fix and avoiding header-splitting heuristic.

maya: update — canary looks good: write syscalls down ~78%, p99 CPU back to normal. closing triage for now, keeping follow-ups on the TODOs above.
liam: great work everyone :thumbsup:
